questions.text: Tell me about a time your analysis changed a business decision.

key_points: Describe the decision being made without data
How you structured the analysis and presented findings
Outcome and business impact of the change
avoid: Analysis done but never acted on

questions.text: Describe a time you found a significant error in a dataset used by the business.

key_points: How you identified the error (anomaly detection, cross-validation)
Steps taken to validate and scope the impact
How you communicated and corrected it

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to explain a complex analysis to a non-technical audience.

key_points: Knew your audience: what they care about
Translated numbers into business language
Used visuals to simplify complexity

questions.text: Describe a time you had to work with incomplete or messy data and what you did.

key_points: Assess quality: what is missing, biased, or noisy
Cleaning and imputation decisions documented
Caveated findings appropriately
avoid: Presenting as if data was perfect

questions.text: Tell me about a time you built a metrics framework from scratch for a product or team.

key_points: Defined north star and supporting metrics
Aligned stakeholders on definitions
Implemented tracking and created dashboards
avoid: Too many metrics with no priority

questions.text: How do you approach writing a SQL query to find duplicate records in a large table?

key_points: GROUP BY + HAVING COUNT > 1 approach
Window functions (ROW_NUMBER) for deduplication
Performance: indexing and partition pruning

questions.text: Explain how you would design a dashboard for monitoring key business KPIs.

key_points: Audience and decision context first
Limit KPIs to actionable leading indicators
Drill-down capability and alert thresholds
avoid: Too many charts with no narrative

questions.text: Walk me through how you would conduct A/B test analysis.

key_points: Sample size and power calculation before launch
Randomisation check and SRM test
Statistical significance vs practical significance
avoid: Stopping test early on first significance

questions.text: How do you handle outliers in a dataset, do you always remove them?

key_points: Understand the source: error vs genuine extreme value
Domain context determines treatment
Document and report whatever decision is made
strong_answer_signals: Sensitivity analysis with and without outliers

questions.text: Describe the difference between correlation and causation with a business example.

key_points: Correlation: two variables move together, no direction claimed
Causation requires controlled experiment or causal inference methods
Real business example where confusion caused bad decisions

questions.text: A stakeholder disagrees with your analysis findings. How do you handle it?

key_points: Understand their objection: data, methodology, or assumption
Walk through the analysis together transparently
Update if their point is valid; hold firm with evidence if not

questions.text: You are asked to deliver an analysis in half the normal time. What do you do?

key_points: Scope negotiation: what question is most critical
Fast-path: existing data, rough cut first
Communicate confidence level of expedited analysis
avoid: Full analysis compressed with no quality signal

questions.text: You discover that a widely used company dashboard has been showing incorrect data for months. What do you do?

key_points: Validate the error thoroughly before raising alarm
Escalate to data team lead and affected business owners immediately
Correct the data, audit decisions made on bad data, document fix
avoid: Waiting to see if anyone notices

questions.text: Two business units are asking for conflicting analyses that require the same data resource. How do you prioritise?

key_points: Understand business impact of each request
Escalate to manager if equal priority
Communicate timeline to both stakeholders

questions.text: You are handed a Python script that produces results no one understands and the author has left. What do you do?

key_points: Run it and document what it produces
Trace logic step by step; add comments
Validate output against known truth; refactor or document

questions.text: What type of analytical problems do you find most engaging?

key_points: Specific domain (customer behaviour, operations, finance)
Why that domain excites you
Connection to this role's data challenges

questions.text: How do you stay current with new tools and techniques in the data space?

key_points: Specific learning channels (papers, blogs, communities)
Tool or technique recently adopted
How applied to current work

questions.text: Why do you want to be a data analyst rather than a data scientist or engineer?

key_points: Clarity on the distinction: business questions vs model building
Your strengths: business intuition, communication, SQL/BI
What you find fulfilling about insight delivery
avoid: 'I couldn't get a data science job'

questions.text: Tell me about a personal or side project involving data you are proud of.

key_points: Problem you chose to investigate and why
Data sources and methods used
Insight or outcome produced
avoid: Copied tutorial with no original thinking

questions.text: How do you ensure the data team's output aligns with business priorities?

key_points: Regular stakeholder alignment sessions
Prioritisation framework tied to business OKRs
Visible roadmap and progress communication

questions.text: How do you build data literacy across a non-technical organisation?

key_points: Assess baseline literacy by team
Training, self-serve dashboards, office hours
Celebrate data-driven wins publicly

questions.text: How would you model customer churn using available transaction data?

key_points: Define churn (no purchase in X days)
Feature engineering: RFM, tenure, product breadth
Model selection and business-friendly output (probability)

questions.text: Tell me about a time you automated a manual reporting process.

key_points: Manual process pain: time, error rate
Automation approach (SQL, Python, BI scheduled report)
Time saved and accuracy improvement

questions.text: Describe how you managed a project where the data you needed was not available.

key_points: Identified alternative proxies or external sources
Communicated limitation to stakeholders
Worked with engineering to instrument missing data

questions.text: Leadership wants to launch a product based on analysis you believe is flawed. What do you do?

key_points: Document your concern with evidence clearly
Escalate through proper channels with urgency proportional to risk
Propose a fast validation to confirm before full launch
strong_answer_signals: Respected final decision with concern on record

questions.text: What is the difference between a data warehouse and a data lake, and when would you use each?

key_points: Warehouse: structured, schema-on-write, BI-optimised
Lake: raw, schema-on-read, flexible for ML and EDA
Lakehouse pattern combines both

questions.text: Tell me about a time you influenced a team to adopt better data practices.

key_points: Identified the pain point (data quality, inconsistent definitions)
Proposed and piloted the improvement
Adoption strategy and outcome

questions.text: How do you validate that a data pipeline is producing correct outputs?

key_points: Row count and null checks
Business rule assertions and range tests
End-to-end reconciliation against source

questions.text: What is the most impactful analysis you have ever done and why?

key_points: Business context and stakes
Your methodology and key finding
Concrete business outcome driven by the insight
strong_answer_signals: Clear causality between insight and action
avoid: Technically impressive but no business impact
